title: Stop losing agents' work: branch-per-agent, no shared-tree banking, restart-resilient landing
what: Diagnose and fix the most expensive recurring failure in the project — agents' pushed work being silently reverted. Test/refute the orchestrator's diagnosis (shared tree is half; shared BRANCH push race is the other half). Research external practice. Answer the owner's two questions. Implement with a --self-test whose arms genuinely disagree. Update HAZARDS.md and CLAUDE.md.
findings: MEASURED 2026-08-14: through 2026-08-13 EVERY commit reaching the integration branch came in as a PR merge from a per-agent codex/* branch (150 such branches on origin). Claude-authored direct commits to the shared branch on 08-09..08-13: ZERO. On 08-14: 117 direct commits, 0 merges.

MEASURED: commits whose message says restore/revert/clobber/lost/dropped/rescue, by day: 08-06 x6, 08-08 x3, 08-10 x4, 08-11 x3, 08-14 x21. The 08-14 spike coincides exactly with the switch from branch-per-agent+PR to shared-tree+shared-branch.
So the answer to the owner's 'did this happen last week' is: not in this form. The scheme that is losing work is one day old.
next_step: Research external practice; build tools/land.mjs with a falsifying --self-test; update HAZARDS + CLAUDE.md; land via plumbing and verify against the remote blob.
